name: Paranormal Shakti frontal session (to lower 'sensitivity')
summary: The frontal-lobe session of Murphy's retired Paranormal Shakti, which the vendor offered to adults troubled by reported paranormal experiences ('victims of paranormal pollution') to lower their 'sensitivity': the same signal on four coils over the forehead. The cited pages name neither the signal nor the length. The hippocampal and amygdala signals in sequence and 30 min are this project's assumptions.
setting: Adults (over 18) only (vendor). Not in sensory deprivation: 'The frontal lobe session should NOT be done in sensory deprivation.' Investigators: not in the 3 days before an investigation, since the vendor says it lowers sensitivity.
schedule: Vendor: after six sessions with the coils over the temporal lobes, three sessions over the frontal lobes; 'This session can be applied once a week for six weeks.' The cited pages give no session length; 30 min is this project's choice. The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days.
notes: The vendor's page: 'Although right-channel coils are shown here, the same signal is used in both channels. ... You need TWO poles (positive and negative) to make ONE magnetic field.' and 'It does not matter which coils are negative and which are positive.' ('The Frontal Lobe Session for Paranormal Shakti', archived 2013-05-09). The cited pages name neither the signal nor the length, so the table of murphy-frontal-reset, with the hippocampal signal first, and the 30 min are assumptions. The page repeats the Feelgood text and photo, so the session may be the one-phase frontal Feelgood session, which starts with the amygdala signal. Coils: Fp1 and AF3 on the left, Fp2 and AF4 on the right (the site names are this project's reading). All four carry the same signal and do not rotate; AF3 and Fp2 are reversed, so each side has both poles. One pass of 9.5 s: the hippocampal signal as a primed burst (one pulse, then four pulses 170 ms later, three times in 0.74 s, after Tsang 2004 p.5 [1017]), 4 s of silence, the amygdala signal, 4 s of silence. Both are rebuilt: the vendor's files are not published. The amygdala signal is the project's rising sweep (6 to 30 Hz) with the published point duration and length (230 points of 3 ms; Ryczko 2002 p.1 [592]). Its point values were never published as numbers. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. The effect is a vendor claim. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users of an earlier version of its signals; if that happens, lower the intensity by one third. Not a treatment for anything: anyone distressed by unusual experiences should talk to a doctor. The product is retired; this program is of historical interest. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
